title: Exam Room
statement:
Simulate one row of `n` exam seats, numbered `0` to `n - 1`, as students come in and leave. Implement the class `ExamRoom`:

- `ExamRoom(n)` sets up the row with all `n` seats empty.
- `seat()` places an arriving student and returns the seat number they take. They choose the empty seat whose distance to the nearest seated student is as large as possible; when several seats tie, they choose the lowest-numbered one. In an empty room they take seat `0`.
- `leave(p)` removes the student sitting in seat `p`. Seat `p` is guaranteed to be occupied.

`seat()` is only called while at least one seat is empty.
constraints: leave(p) is only called when seat p is occupied
At most 10^4 calls in total are made to seat and leave
notes:
## Intuition

A new student only cares about gaps between neighbours. Before the first occupied seat, the best spot is seat `0`, at distance `seats[0]`. After the last, it is seat `n - 1`. Inside a gap between neighbours `a < b`, the best spot is the middle `a + floor((b - a) / 2)`, at distance `floor((b - a) / 2)`. Keeping the occupied seats in a sorted list lets one left-to-right scan compare all these gaps. Because `n` can be 10^9, the empty seats themselves are never listed; a brute force that tries every seat only works for tiny rows.

## Approach

1. Store the occupied seats in a sorted array `seats`.
2. `seat()`: in an empty room, take seat `0`.
3. Otherwise start with seat `0` as `best`, at distance `seats[0]`.
4. For each pair of neighbours, compute `distance = floor(gap / 2)`; if it is strictly larger than `bestDistance`, the middle seat becomes `best` and `insertAt` remembers where it goes in the array.
5. Seat `n - 1` wins only if its distance `n - 1 - last` is strictly larger.
6. Insert `best` at `insertAt` and return it.
7. `leave(p)`: binary search for `p` in `seats` and remove it.

Strict comparisons while scanning left to right give the lowest seat on ties.

## Example 1, step by step

With `n = 10`: the room is empty, so seat `0`. Then `seats = [0]`: the left end gives distance 0 and seat 9 gives 9, so seat `9`. With `[0, 9]` the middle is `0 + 4 = 4`. With `[0, 4, 9]` both gaps give distance 2; the first one wins, seat `2`. After `leave(4)`, `seats = [0, 2, 9]`: the gap `2..9` gives distance 3 at seat `5`.

## Complexity

- Time: `seat()` is O(k) for the scan and insertion, where k is the number of seated students; `leave` is O(log k) to find the seat plus O(k) to remove it.
- Space: O(k) for `seats`.

## Pitfalls

- Use `>`, not `>=`, so ties keep the lower seat.
- The two ends are special: their distance is the whole stretch to the nearest student, not half of it.
- Never allocate an array of `n` seats; `n` can be 10^9.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `n` | number of seats in the row |
| `seats` | occupied seat numbers, sorted |
| `best`, `bestDistance` | best seat found so far and its distance to the nearest student |
| `insertAt` | index in `seats` where `best` belongs |
| `distance` | best distance available inside the gap between two neighbours |
| `last` | the highest occupied seat |
| `left`, `right`, `mid` | binary search bounds used by `leave` |

narration.4: Only the occupied seats are stored, kept in increasing order.
narration.9: In an empty room the student takes seat 0.
narration.13: Start with seat 0, whose distance is the stretch before the first student.
narration.16: Walk over every pair of neighbouring students.
narration.17: The middle of this gap is floor(gap / 2) away from both neighbours.
narration.18: Strictly larger, so on ties the earlier (lower) seat stays chosen.
narration.20: The new seat is the middle of this gap.
narration.24: The last occupied seat decides how far the right end is.
narration.25: Seat n - 1 wins only if it is strictly farther than everything before it.
narration.29: Insert the chosen seat where it keeps the array sorted.
narration.30: Report the seat the student took.
narration.37: Binary search for the position of seat p in the sorted list.
narration.39: If the seat at mid is below p, p must lie to its right.
narration.45: left now points at seat p; remove it from the sorted list.
